summary: In an ordinary goose session, plain code runs a fixed list of steps around the AI model's calls, and a plain text reply with no tool request ends the turn when nothing else is set up. A goal (/goal or /grind), a recipe's checks or required output, or a plugin's stop hook can each cause more work before the turn ends.

judgments.question: The model stopped; has it delivered the recipe's final output, or must it be told to?
judgments.answer: Only for a recipe with a response schema: code looks since your kickoff message for a final-output call that succeeded. If there is one the turn may end; otherwise it adds a model-only message saying to call that tool now, and the agent continues.

judgments.question: If a review pass or check crashed or returned garbage, does the review say so?
judgments.answer: On goose review's default path, a failed check or per-file pass adds no findings and a warning on stderr. If the review otherwise completes, it prints the findings that pass the severity floor and exits successfully.

judgments.question: When a subagent stops, did it complete, fail or get cancelled?
judgments.answer: After reloading its session, code checks in a fixed order: a successful final-output call means Completed, even if the run was cancelled or errored afterwards; else a cancelled run is Cancelled; anything else is Failed.

judgments.question: Has the agent taken as many steps as it may without coming back to you?
judgments.answer: When this step is reached, code counts the assistant turns kept since your kickoff message; at the budget it ends the turn with a fixed "Would you like me to continue?" message. In an ordinary session the budget is the session's max_turns, else GOOSE_MAX_TURNS, else 1000.

judgments.question: Has the conversation grown big enough to summarise before the next model call?
judgments.answer: Code compares the conversation's tokens with the context limit and compacts above a threshold: by default 0.8 of the limit, or 225,000 tokens if that is less, and both are settings. A threshold of 0 or less, or 1 or more, turns this trigger off, and it is not built when the provider manages its own context.

judgments.question: When the conversation is compacted, what is carried forward?
judgments.answer: The session's own model writes the summary. If its reply parses as the structured summary and renders to non-empty text, that rendering is used; otherwise the raw reply is kept unchanged.

judgments.question: How long may a command from the developer shell tool run?
judgments.answer: The model may pass a timeout with each call; if it does not, code uses a setting, else 300 seconds. A value of 0 means that tool sets no deadline.

judgments.question: When a resumed command-line session's original provider cannot start, what runs instead?
judgments.answer: Only on resume with no --provider flag, and only when the provider's error text contains one of three fixed phrases, code switches to the globally configured provider and model and prints a yellow warning. Any other provider error, or a failed fallback, exits.

judgments.question: Can a subagent start subagents of its own?
judgments.answer: No. Code refuses a delegate call from a subagent session and does not list the tool to a session it identifies as a subagent, so delegation depth is fixed at one.

judgments.question: Did a file edit find exactly the text the model meant to replace?
judgments.answer: Code counts exact occurrences of the model's before text: exactly one goes on to be replaced and written; zero or more than one returns an error and writes nothing. There is no fuzzy or whitespace-tolerant matching.

problems.title: The --max-tool-repetitions flag has no effect
problems.plain: goose's help says this flag limits consecutive identical tool calls. At this commit it does not: the command line accepts the value but never passes it to the repetition check, and the agent's standard setup gives that check no limit, so it never refuses a repeated call. goose's tracker has an open issue about how this limit should work, where contributors discuss wiring it up or removing it.

problems.title: By default, a failed review check still exits successfully
problems.plain: On goose review's default path, a check or per-file pass that fails, panics or returns output that cannot be parsed adds no findings and prints a warning on stderr. If the review otherwise completes it exits successfully, with nothing on stdout or in the exit status to mark the failed check.

problems.title: No code reads a verdict on a /goal
problems.plain: After /goal, goose says the agent will verify the goal before finishing. That check is left to the model: when code later clears the goal, it reads no verdict from the reply.
